genimage_tiny_attribution.description: Tiny GenImage source attribution with the benchmark train/validation split used in Table 1.

accuracy.description: Overall source-attribution accuracy on the Tiny GenImage validation slice.

balanced_accuracy.description: Mean per-class recall, which catches shortcuts that improve common classes while sacrificing harder generators.

precision_weighted.description: Weighted precision for source attribution, retaining continuity with the original aggregate classification report.

recall_weighted.description: Weighted recall for source attribution, retaining continuity with the original aggregate classification report.

f1_weighted.description: Weighted F1 for source attribution, combining precision and recall at the aggregate class distribution.

f1_macro.description: Unweighted macro F1, which rewards methods that improve all generator classes rather than only the easiest ones.

worst_class_recall.description: Lowest per-class recall, included to expose methods that abandon a difficult source class.

feature_count.description: Descriptor dimensionality, used as a machine-independent compactness constraint.

genimage_tiny_binary.description: Tiny GenImage real-vs-fake classification on the same split, testing whether source attribution features also support binary synthetic-image detection.

accuracy.description: Overall real-vs-fake accuracy on the Tiny GenImage validation slice.

balanced_accuracy.description: Average of real-image and fake-image recall, guarding against single-side binary shortcuts.

precision_weighted.description: Weighted precision for the binary real-vs-fake task.

recall_weighted.description: Weighted recall for the binary real-vs-fake task.

f1_weighted.description: Weighted F1 for the binary real-vs-fake task.

f1_macro.description: Unweighted macro F1, exposing methods that trade away either real or fake recall.

worst_class_recall.description: Lower of real-image recall and fake-image recall.

feature_count.description: Descriptor dimensionality, used as a machine-independent compactness constraint.
